title: Utility Specification Outline Template
description: The standard U.S. utility specification outline runs: title, cross-reference to related applications, background (field + prior art problems), summary, brief description of the drawings, detailed description, claims, abstract, and drawings. The detailed description must enable a person of ordinary skill to make and use the invention (35 U.S.C. 112). The template keeps each section's job separate so enablement, novelty, and claim support each have a home.
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Independent Claim Template
description: The independent claim template follows the classic three-part form: preamble (the category — 'A widget comprising:'), transitional phrase ('comprising' for open, 'consisting of' for closed), and the body reciting elements in a logical order with antecedent basis ('a lever... said lever'). One independent claim per invention core keeps the claim set readable; everything else hangs off it as dependents.
demo:
claim = '1. A widget comprising:\na lever pivotally mounted to a base;\na spring biasing said lever toward said base.'
print(claim)
print('check: preamble -> transition (comprising) -> elements with antecedent basis')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Dependent Claim Template
description: 'The widget of claim 1, wherein...' — the dependent claim template narrows by adding a limitation, specifying a material, or reciting an alternative embodiment. Good dependent sets form a fallback ladder: if prior art knocks out the broad claim, the narrower ones still stand. Each dependent claim must further limit its parent; a dependent that merely restates the parent is rejected as indefinite or redundant.
demo:
print('2. The widget of claim 1, wherein said spring is a coil spring.')
print('3. The widget of claim 2, wherein said coil spring is stainless steel.')
print('ladder: broad -> narrower -> narrowest (fallback positions)')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Method Claim Template
description: Method claims recite steps in active voice and chronological order: 'A method of X, the method comprising: receiving...; processing...; outputting....' Each step should name its actor implicitly (the system) and its inputs and outputs explicitly, so infringement can be mapped to observable acts. Means-plus-function language is avoided in steps unless 112(f) treatment is intended and the structure is in the specification.
demo:
print('1. A method of sorting parcels, the method comprising:')
print('   scanning a label on a parcel;')
print('   routing the parcel based on the scanned label.')
print('steps: active voice, chronological, observable acts')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Means-Plus-Function Template (112f)
description: Under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), 'means for fastening' without recited structure is construed to cover only the corresponding structure described in the specification and its equivalents. The template therefore pairs every means clause with a specification section naming the structure (screw, latch, weld) — otherwise the claim is indefinite. Use 112(f) deliberately for breadth-with-anchor, never accidentally.
demo:
print('claim: ...means for fastening the panel to the frame...')
print('spec MUST describe: screw 14 / latch 16 / weld (the corresponding structure)')
print('no structure in spec -> indefinite under 112(f)')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Design Patent Figure Description Template
description: The design application template lists each figure — FIG. 1 front view, FIG. 2 rear view, FIG. 3 left side, FIG. 4 right side, FIG. 5 top, FIG. 6 bottom, FIG. 7 perspective — with a one-line brief description per figure. Broken lines show unclaimed environment; solid lines show the claimed design. The template enforces that every visible line is either claimed (solid) or disclaimed (broken), never ambiguous.
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Plant Patent Specification Template
description: The plant patent template carries: Latin name, variety denomination, parentage, the location and conditions of discovery or breeding, detailed botanical description (habit, foliage, flower, fruit) with color references, and the asexual reproduction statement with dates. Color photographs substitute for formal drawings. The single claim reads: 'A new and distinct variety of [plant] as described and illustrated.'
demo:
print('sections: Latin name, parentage, discovery, botanical description, asexual reproduction')
print('claim: A new and distinct variety of rose plant as described and illustrated.')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Provisional Application Template
description: The provisional template needs a cover sheet (inventor names, title, correspondence address), the full written description with at least one drawing figure, and the filing fee — no claims required, though one informal claim helps focus. The template's critical warning: the provisional only protects what it actually describes, so thin provisionals are worse than none because they create false confidence about the priority date.
demo:
print('provisional package: cover sheet + full description + figure(s) + fee')
print('warning: priority covers ONLY what the provisional actually describes')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: PCT Request Outline Template
description: The PCT request (Form PCT/RO/101) template covers: applicant and inventor data, the title, priority claims with dates and countries, the choice of International Searching Authority, and designation of all contracting states (automatic). The template pairs the request with the description, claims, abstract, and drawings in the required order, and calendars the 30-month national-phase deadline from day one.
demo:
print('PCT/RO/101: parties, title, priority claims, ISA choice, auto-designation')
print('calendar on filing day: 30-month national-phase deadline')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Abstract Template (150 Words)
description: The abstract template produces a single paragraph under 150 words stating the technical field, the problem, the solution's essence, and the principal use — never marketing language, never claims language. Examiners and searchers read the abstract first, so it must let a stranger decide in thirty seconds whether the document matters to them. The template ends with a word-count check.
demo:
abstract = ('A widget for fastening panels. Existing fasteners require tools. The widget provides a ' 'spring-biased lever that engages a slot without tools, cutting installation time. Useful in ' 'furniture and equipment housings.')
print(abstract)
print('words:', len(abstract.split()), '(must be <= 150)')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Background Section Template
description: The background template has two lawful jobs: state the field of the invention, and describe the problems in the prior art that the invention solves — without admitting that any particular reference is prior art against the applicant. The template's red flag: never characterize the applicant's own earlier work as prior art, and never use the background to argue patentability; that belongs in prosecution, not the specification.
demo:
print('background: (1) field of invention, (2) problems in prior approaches')
print('red flags: no admissions; no patentability argument here')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Brief Description of Drawings Template
description: The template gives each figure one sentence — 'FIG. 1 is a perspective view of the widget; FIG. 2 is a cross-section taken along line 2-2 of FIG. 1' — in figure-number order. It cross-checks that every figure number in the text exists in the drawings and vice versa, the single most common formal defect in new filings. Reference numerals introduced here must match the detailed description exactly.
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Drawing Sheet Guide (USPTO Margins)
description: The USPTO drawing sheet guide: 8.5-by-11-inch flexible white sheets, margins of at least 2.5 cm top and left and 1.5 cm right and bottom (1 cm for the right/bottom on some sheets — the template uses the safe values), black ink lines, reference numerals at least 0.32 cm high, no shading that obscures lines. The template includes a margin-check routine because defective drawings draw some of the most avoidable office actions in prosecution.
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Inventor Declaration Template
description: The inventor's oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63) template states the inventor believes themselves to be the original inventor, acknowledges the duty of disclosure, and authorizes the application. Since the America Invents Act, the declaration can be filed later in prosecution, and assignment documents can carry the required statements. The template warns: inventorship is a legal fact about who conceived, not a reward list — wrong inventors can invalidate the patent.
demo:
print('declaration: original inventor belief + duty of disclosure')
print('warning: inventorship = who conceived; wrong names risk invalidity')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Information Disclosure Statement Template
description: The IDS template (Form SB/08) lists every material reference the applicant knows — U.S. patents, publications, foreign documents — with copies of non-U.S. documents, filed to satisfy the duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.56. The template's timing rules: file with the application or within three months to avoid fees; late IDS filings need the fee and a certification. Intentionally withholding material art can render the patent unenforceable.
demo:
print('SB/08: list every material reference known to applicant')
print('timing: with filing or within 3 months (fee-free); duty under 37 CFR 1.56')
provenance: Public reference: USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) and uspto.gov; verified 2026-10-21.
